title: Software Becomes Free to Copy
subtitle: In one month, a solo developer cloned seven Adobe apps and a hobby project started turning PS5 games into PC programs. This is my guess at what happens next, and where the value goes when copying costs nothing.
summary: AnyPS5 and the ArtCraft Adobe clones show copying getting cheap. Where does value move next, and where do I stand?
author: Samartha

questions.a: A story about how the next four years might go once AI makes rebuilding software cheap. The first chapter is reported from the news. Every chapter after it is my forecast, labelled as such.

questions.q: Why does it matter to me?
questions.a: If code stops being a moat, the skills and bets that made sense for my parents' generation of programmers stop making sense for me. I want to see where the value moves before I commit years to anything.
Not very. The direction feels solid; the speed is a guess. The dashboard numbers after October 2026 are my estimates, not data.
A court ruling that AI-assisted 'clean-room' rebuilds infringe copyright, or the clones stalling in alpha for a year. Either would slow everything in this story down.
